opti-2: Dawn in the Everglades. A soft white mist floats over the grass.
opti-3: At Lake Woodruff, mist curls up off the water.
opti-4: Cold air, and a white cloud sits on the lake.
opti-5: Sunny and warm? The cloud is gone.
opti-6: In winter, manatees crowd into Blue Spring. Its water stays warm all year.
opti-7: On cold mornings, mist rises off the spring, like steam from a pot.
opti-9: What happens to water when you heat it up or cool it down?
27-02-welcome: Our film starts on a misty Florida morning. First, inspect a cold cup with a secret on the outside.
27-02-lesson: Today you're a water scientist. Heat a pot, test two drinks, then climb down a steam tower.
27-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
27-02-assign: Time to show your data. Fill in the table, then draw your Pot Lab comic.
how-27-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the cup, then tap three things you notice.
how-27-02-compare: Put the lid on one specimen and the paper towel on the other: drag them, or tap one, then a specimen. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-27-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-27-02-det: Pick three files, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name the change. Predict if it was warming up or cooling down, and watch the place appear.
how-27-02-partc: Draw a comic strip with four panels showing the Pot Lab: ice, melted water, boiling water with steam, and drops on a cool lid. In each panel, draw the water and label its state: solid, liquid, gas, liquid again.
